items.title: Radhakishan Damani portfolio: Top 10 stock holdings of the ace investor
items.description: DMart founder and ace investor Radhakishan Damani is among India’s richest stock market investors, with his family’s net worth estimated at over $20 billion, according to Forbes. Popularly known as the “retail king of India”, the billionaire publicly holds 14 stocks. Here are his top 10 stock holdings by value, based on data from Trendlyne.

items.title: Indians remit $2.7 billion overseas in August, led by travel
items.description: Outward remittances under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS) stood at $2.7 billion, with travel accounting for the largest chunk. Indians spent $1.6 billion on travel in August, from $1.7 billion in July, while $275 million were spent on maintenan-ce of relatives. Indian citizen spent $321 million on investments in equity and debt, while $191 million on studies abroad.

items.title: Gross FDI inflows to India fall to $11 billion in August
items.description: Gross foreign direct investment (FDI) to India decreased to $11 billion in August, from $14 billion a month ago. Net FDI to India slows $3 billion in August, from $7 billion in July. Financial services, communication services, computer services and manufacturing accounted for around 73% of total FDI equity inflows during April-August 2026.

items.title: Swiggy sinks 16% to record low as quick-commerce losses widen
items.description: Shares of Swiggy fell by 16.4% to ₹176.70, marking a record low for the company. This decline raises concerns over cash burn and achieving profitability in its quick-commerce business. Analysts are questioning Swiggy's strategic choices and execution following its market debut. The widening losses in the quick-commerce segment have drawn attention to the company's overall performance.

items.title: BSE begins hunt for MD & CEO successor ahead of 2027 exit
items.description: BSE has initiated the search for its next managing director and chief executive officer. Sundararaman Ramamurthy is scheduled to retire in June 2027 after reaching the age limit. The exchange is looking for candidates with at least 20 years of experience, which includes senior leadership roles. Applicants need to be under 62 years old as of July 1, 2027.

items.title: Small and midcap indices post worst weekly decline in two years
items.description: Mid-cap and small-cap stocks in India have faced major declines, indicating a shift in market sentiment. The Nifty MidCap 150 and Small-cap 250 indices reported their worst weekly falls in two years. Domestic retail investors initially supported these segments by increasing mutual fund contributions. However, concerns over rising oil prices and fiscal deficits are adding to market uncertainties.

items.title: Private sector activity hits four month high in October
items.description: India's private sector activity experienced significant growth in October, reaching a four-month high as new orders increased. The HSBC Flash India Composite Purchasing Managers' Index rose to 56.7, signaling expansion. Manufacturing output and new orders remained stable, while services activity saw notable improvement. Employment increased slightly, although firms showed caution in hiring due to adequate staffing levels. International demand contributed to growth, with export orders expanding significantly during this period.

items.title: Target reached, but asset monetisation to continue: DIPAM secretary Arunish Chawla
items.description: "We have already identified a cluster of 10 national highways, which will provide the underlying capital asset. So, the second public InvITs is in the works and hopefully before the close of this financial year, it will also come to fruition," Chawla said. "We are also bringing down the equity (stake) in nationalised banks gradually to the minimum public shareholding norm of 75%, that is part of the mandate that we have to share the wealth with the people and also in line with regulations...we are moving ahead on that path."

items.title: RBI flags rising inflation risks from West Asia conflict, El Nino despite resilient Indian economy
items.description: India's external sector shows resilience due to a narrowing trade gap and comfortable foreign exchange reserves. Inflationary pressures have intensified due to geopolitical tensions and supply-side bottlenecks. The RBI reported an increase in both industry and services indicators, showcasing economic strength. The IMF has revised India's growth projection for 2026-27 to 7% based on resilient domestic demand. Global financial volatility has increased amid global challenges and rising inflation risks.

items.title: Zetwerk’s early backers sit on up to 36x returns post listing
items.description: The listing provides liquidity for investors who backed an industrial business when venture funding largely favoured software and consumer internet companies. The shares closed at Rs 138.30 on the BSE, 8.4% below the Rs 151 issue price, valuing Zetwerk at Rs 23,432 crore. They opened at Rs 159, a 5.3% premium.
